title: Time and daily actions
japaneseTitle: みんなの日本語 第4課
summary: Say when things happen, define time ranges, and move polite verbs between non-past and past.
sourceFiles: みんなの日本語　第4課.pdf
takeaways: Exact clock times take に; relative times usually do not.
から and まで independently mark the start and end of a range.
ました and ませんでした place an action in the past.

grammar.title: Pin an action to a time
grammar.summary: Use に with exact points such as clock times and calendar dates.

examples.english: I wake up at seven thirty every morning.

examples.note: Weekdays may use に or omit it.

grammar.caution: 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日, 今朝 and similar relative times normally omit に.

grammar.title: Draw a time span
grammar.pattern: Time から Time まで
grammar.summary: から marks the starting boundary and まで marks the ending boundary. Either can stand alone.

examples.english: I work from nine until five.
The lunch break is until one.

grammar.title: Ask and answer about the past
grammar.summary: Use ました for an affirmative past action and ませんでした for a negative past action.

tokens.reading: べんきょうしませんでした

recall.answer: Normally no. Relative/repeating time words do not need に.

recall.prompt: What marks the end of a time range?
